thread:
support_anna: Heads-up — customer ACME reported a sudden p95/p99 jump after we rolled runtime 3.1.4 to eu-west about 00:30 UTC. They see embeddings latency 100ms -> ~850ms. Happened ~28m after rollout. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/acme/embeds :eyes:
claire_cs: ugh, they just called support. any quick mitigation we can apply?
raj_oncall: Oncall here — are errors spiking or just latency?
support_anna: no 5xxs, just long tail. p50 stable. p95/p99 exploded. sample req ids: req_9a2f, req_9a3a, req_9b00.
mei_runtime: I rolled 3.1.4 globally in eu-west earlier. change summary: small KV-cache commit-ordering shim + a kernel selector tweak for short sequences. Canary looked ok on our synthetic, but prod cohorts differ.
tom_sre: can we get flamegraphs/trace for one of the slow reqs? stack traces?
support_anna: pasted a short trace from req_9a2f: ```
2024-07-12T00:14:02Z TRACE call=req_9a2f runtime:kernel_selector.cpp:142 selectKernel() took 412ms
2024-07-12T00:14:02Z TRACE call=req_9a2f runtime:kvcache.cpp:311 commitPrefix() waited 328ms on lock
2024-07-12T00:14:02Z INFO call=req_9a2f total_token_time 780ms
```
raj_oncall: looks like kernel selector + KV commit contention both high. does telemetry show lock contention spikes?
mei_runtime: checking. initial sweep: host kernel_select_ms median unchanged; 95/99 climbed. Also seeing increased mutex waits in kvcache. Hypothesis: the shim reordered commits which increased lock hold time for short requests, causing queueing that amplifies P99.
claire_cs: is this cohort-specific? ACME uses short-embedding requests (~64 tokens) and high QPS.
mei_runtime: yes that matches. Continuous batching + longer KV lock holds = head-of-line blocking for short requests.
tom_sre: mitigation options: 1) rollback 3.1.4 in eu-west (fast but disruptive), 2) flip kernel selector to legacy path, 3) temporarily narrow traffic to older runtime via routing split, 4) increase per-host worker threads/autoscale threshold. Which is fastest?
raj_oncall: can we flip selector remotely without deploy? we have runtime flag gate for selector: `runtime.selector=v2` -> `v1`.
mei_runtime: yes feature flag exists. I'll test flip on one canary host now.
deploy-bot: deploy event: feature-flag-toggle by mei_runtime at 1775010400 — runtime.selector -> v1 on host eu-west-3a-canary
mei_runtime: canary flip observed: p99 dropped from 840ms -> 140ms on that host within ~90s.
support_anna: customer confirms latency improved on requests routed to that host.
claire_cs: awesome. can we roll that to all eu-west hosts?
mei_runtime: I'm preparing a staged flag sweep: canary -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Will monitor tail. If safe, leave flag in place and we can later revert the shim in code and re-roll.
tom_sre: while sweeping, set autoscale buffer +1 and increase socket backlog for embeddings route. Add temporary route-slew to prefer hosts with v1 selector.
raj_oncall: also capture a diff trace to bisect later: run A/B on v1 vs v2 under production traffic and dump kernel selection timings, lock hold times, and batch sizes. Put sampling at higher rate for 30m.
mei_runtime: agreed. I'll create perf collection job: `perf-collect --cohort=search-embed --samples=1000 --fields=kernel_ms,lock_us,batch_size` and push to /tmp/triage/1775009999.tar.gz
support_anna: next steps for customer: informed ACME that we have a mitigation (selector flag) rolling and we'll follow up with root cause and a timeline. They are okay for now but asking for RCA.
claire_cs: good. please cc me on post-mortem so I can update CSM notes.
mei_runtime: plan: 1) finish flag sweep and confirm stabilized p95/p99 for 60m, 2) run bisect between shim vs selector in controlled A/B, 3) if shim is root cause, revert shim and validate, 4) if selector change interacts badly with short tails, add a short-request fast-path to avoid locking. I'll produce a short writeup.
tom_sre: add an incident tag `latency-1775009999` and retention of traces for 7d. Also notify infra about potential autoscale changes.
raj_oncall: thanks team. keeping oncall looped. If p99 resurges, rollback to 3.1.3 and open priority hotfix.
mei_runtime: flag sweep 20% -> 50% done, p99 trending down. Will update in 10m. :thumbsup: 
support_anna: customer updated: appreciate the fast response. will ping if they see any regression.
mei_runtime: (final) full sweep complete at 1775011700, p99 back to baseline. created follow-up PR to revert shim + add unit test for commit ordering. filing postmortem doc.
claire_cs: great work — please drop a short summary in #customer-notifications once RCA is ready. :shipit:
